items.title: A battered stock market looks for the bottom: What to watch this week
items.summary: After a week headlined by the Anthropic IPO and the long-awaited release of GTA VI, the upcoming five-day stretch should be a bit calmer.

items.title: GTA VI Broke Every Record in 24 Hours, So Why Did Take-Two Shareholders Sell?
items.summary: Rockstar posted a record-shattering launch and a near-perfect review score, yet Take-Two investors headed for the exits. The real money behind this franchise sits somewhere the day-one sales figures never touch, and it has not even launched.

items.title: Roblox Soars 9% as Oppenheimer Says GTA VI Hasn’t Dented Engagement, Lifts Target to $55
items.summary: Key TakeawaysRoblox shares jumped 9% after Oppenheimer raised its target to $55 from $50, saying GTA VI hasn’t materially hurt engagement. That eases the worry behind Roblox’s fourth-quarter guide, which built in a headwind from Take-Two Interactive’s GTA VI.

items.title: GTA VI Hype More Than Doubled Sony’s US PS5 And Microsoft’s Xbox Weekly Sales, Circana Says
items.summary: The firm said PlayStation 5 sales were more than 2.4 times higher than a year earlier during the week ended Nov. 7, while Xbox Series sales rose to 2.3 times their year-ago level.

items.title: Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia: Long or short accountability?
items.summary:
Market Hang tackles the top stories of the day. Including Nvidia's board unanimously reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO and what the White House's involvement says about accountability in corporate America, whether the government has effectively put a floor under the AI trade, and Anthropic falling as options on the stock begin trading for the first time.

The panel, with Yahoo Finance's Julie Hyman, debates where everyone sits on a one-to-five bullishness scale, whether this is a stock picker's market or a CapEx bubble that precedes a secular bear, the risk of a politically driven slowdown in data center construction, and OpenAI's chief scientist calling for a speed limit on AI development, including whether an FDA-style regulator is the right model for AI.
